claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is homogenized, single-phase, and has minimal pre-existing long-range order.
Rapid thermal cycling accentuates differential thermal expansion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Differential thermal expansion during thermal cycling generates localized internal stresses.
Thermally generated internal stresses drive short-range atomic ordering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermal processing can generate localized compositional fluctuations in the HfNbTaTiZr system.
Short-range ordering or localized compositional fluctuations alter dislocation behavior.
Short-range ordering or localized compositional fluctuations alter lattice interactions.
Thermally induced ordering or compositional fluctuations increase the alloy's creep resistance at approximately 1250 °C.
Thermally induced ordering or compositional fluctuations modify aging-induced hardening at 600–800 °C.
Thermally induced ordering or compositional fluctuations modify the temperature dependence of elastic modulus between 293 and 1100 K.
Thermally cycled specimens will exhibit stronger short-range-order or compositional-fluctuation signatures than baseline specimens.
TEM or advanced diffraction can quantify the proposed short-range ordering or compositional fluctuations.
Elastic modulus is to be measured from 293 to 1100 K.
Aging-induced hardening is to be measured after treatments at 600–800 °C.
Tensile creep behavior is to be measured at approximately 1250 °C.
A control processed identically except for slow thermal ramps can isolate the effects of aggressive thermal cycling.
